plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aligns with the conservative mandate of cutting leverage and favoring quality.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and lowering concentration.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small positions to reduce overall leverage.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.
Buy ERX at 4% as a strong scanner long setup to add growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces leverage while adding a high-conviction long setup, aiming for moderate drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.
Add to existing leveraged positions (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase growth potential.
Buy ERX at 6% as a strong scanner long setup, leveraging high conviction.
This plan leans into higher risk for potentially higher returns, using strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, which can lead to larger drawdowns and daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes steady income and low drawdown over growth.
It aims to park cash for yield, understanding distributions are variable.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces growth potential and high-beta exposure, aiming for low drawdown. NAV can still fall in a selloff.
